incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57 — ss. 10-14 (incorporation), s. 52 (issue of shares), s. 102 (registered records office), s. 157 (directors' resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) together with Notice of Articles (Form 2) filed under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the BCBCA; shares without par value may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine, and no escrow deposit or capital blocking account is required for a general business corporation. Fully paid status must be completed on issuance; non-resident share subscriptions do not trigger escrow absent a prescribed class of shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned first director(s) hereby resolve: 1. The Corporation accepts the share subscriptions and issues 1,000 common shares without par value to the sole subscriber, fully paid. 2. The registered records office is fixed at [address, British Columbia], and the records agent is appointed. 3. [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. 4. The officers are authorized to open bank accounts with [Bank] and execute banking and commercial contracts for the Corporation. Adopted pursuant to the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca) / NUANS service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search through Corporate Online or an approved provider to confirm the proposed name is distinguishable; submit a Name Reservation Request containing the primary name and two alternate names; pay the online reservation fee; the reservation remains valid for 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, file a revised Name Reservation Request addressing the Registrar's stated objections; contest a conflicting name through the Registry's objection procedure within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2) electronically, specifying the registered records office address in British Columbia, the share structure, first directors, and any special resolutions; pay the CAD 350 filing fee; sign and deliver electronically; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form 3) for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file a corrective filing or amended Notice of Articles via Corporate Online within 30 days of the defect notice; resubmit any corrected forms for re-registration without re-payment of the full fee where the defect is ministerial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a federal Business Number (BN) and open required tax accounts, including GST/HST (if taxable supply exceeds CAD 30,000), corporate income tax, and payroll deductions if employees are hired; provide the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles; confirm director identification and any non-resident director status.
required_dossiers: Directors' full names and residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA issues a query on the registration, respond through My Business Account or the CRA business enquiries line within 30 days; supply certified corporate documents and corrected beneficial ownership information to reactivate the account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records, Minute Book, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registered records office / corporate secretary within British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution; issue share certificates to the subscriber in accordance with the Notice of Articles; open and maintain the corporate minute book, share register, directors' register, and officers' register; ensure all consents and resolutions are executed and retained at the registered records office in British Columbia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defective share issuance or register entry by supplemental board resolution and amend the corporate registers; file corrected records promptly to maintain statutory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and KYC Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank commercial banking centre (e.g., BMO, RBC, TD, Scotiabank, CIBC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present certified corporate documents to the commercial branch; complete the account application, beneficial ownership declaration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and signatory authority forms; undergo KYC verification of directors and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Banking resolution from the first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a current good standing certificate, obtain it from BC Registries and Online Services and resubmit with any updated resolution clarifying signatory authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure offshore BIM/CAD drafting under NAICS 541330; Engineers and Geoscientists British Columbia (EGBC) would only mandate a Certificate of Authorization if professional engineering services are provided; municipal business licensing office applies to any physical office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (non-industrial office); no provincial manufacturing, operating, or professional engineering permit required for the core drafting service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy; Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (federal)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based BIM/CAD operations generate no reportable contaminants; no environmental assessment certificate required under the Environmental Assessment Act (SBC 2002, c. 43).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge; applicable thresholds are limited to municipal sanitary sewer bylaws, BC Recycling Regulation for electronic waste disposal, and general solid waste handling; no VOC or wastewater discharge limits apply to IT office operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with the BC Fire Code (fire extinguishers, exit signage, fire safety plan), BC Building Code structural and occupancy permits for the leased office, and WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and workplace clearance for employees.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with prudential oversight by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign exchange policy is administered under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and the Bank of Canada Act. Canada has no dedicated exchange-control agency; FINTRAC supervises cross-border financial transaction reporting for AML purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full and unrestricted convertibility for both current account and capital account transactions under a free-floating CAD regime. Profit remittance is unrestricted: dividends may be paid and transferred outward after BCBCA solvency tests are met, subject only to federal Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, reduced by applicable income tax treaty) and bank/FINTRAC reporting of cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000. No Central Bank permit, genuine-transaction test, or exchange-control approval is required for dividend, interest, or service-fee repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, or repatriation timeline for export or service-export proceeds under the Currency Act. Invoices may be denominated and settled in USD or any freely convertible currency; a CAD-denominated operating account and a separate USD sub-account may be maintained simultaneously. Cross-border electronic transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC by the financial institution as large cross-border EFT reports. Retained foreign currency may be held indefinitely and converted at prevailing market rates without restriction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Business Chequing) + USD Supplemental Account
Operational Account (Business Chequing) with Cross-Border USD Rail (BMO Harris)
Operational Account (Business Chequing) + Global Transfer Wire Rail
Operational Account (Business Chequing) + US Dollar Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as an auxiliary rail; low as a primary treasury account. Wise (registered as a Money Service Business with FINTRAC and compliant with the BC Money Services Businesses Act) may be used for low-value cross-border disbursements and multi-currency settlement. Offshore electronic money institutions without FINTRAC registration or without compliance with the federal Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), supervised by the Bank of Canada, cannot lawfully hold or settle CAD for Canadian resident corporations. Primary corporate banking should remain with a CDIC-insured Schedule I bank; EMI balances are uninsured and unsuitable for capital escrow or large wire aggregation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically in Canada for corporate account opening. Tier-1 banks support fully remote onboarding for corporations whose directors are Canadian residents or residents of recognized low-risk treaty jurisdictions, using digital identity verification, video interview, and electronic signature. Non-resident directors from non-treaty or higher-risk jurisdictions will generally be subject to enhanced due diligence and may be asked to attend a Vancouver branch in person or to provide notarized and apostilled true-copy identification through a Canadian counsel. Practical recommendation: appoint a BC-resident director or instruct BC counsel to attend the initial banker interview while non-resident directors submit notarized certified copies and a board resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding foreign passports from higher-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of passports; proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement); BC corporate registry extract (Current); apostilled Certificate of Good Standing; scanned articles of incorporation; beneficial ownership register identifying all UBOs; source-of-funds declaration; board resolution appointing the banker and signing officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border EPC or infrastructure clients remitting large episodic USD settlements without a verifiable services contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed BIM/structural drafting master service agreement aligned to ISIC 7110 scope; project SOW and milestone schedule; verified commercial invoice ledger with unique invoice numbers; client UBO and corporate registry profile; deliverable acceptance emails or transmittal logs; evidence of professional liability insurance if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inward capital injection followed within days by outward disbursements to foreign subcontractors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; corporate resolutions authorizing share issuance; bank source-of-funds letter from the remitting institution; subcontractor agreements with itemized invoices; FX conversion tracker; projected monthly treasury reconciliation; FINTRAC compliant wire reference coding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receiving settlement from a third party other than the named contract counterparty (factoring, pass-through, or intermediary payment)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written client payment attribution letter; assignment of receivables notice or factoring agreement if applicable; AML questionnaire responses explaining the tripartite payment chain; uniform invoice naming convention matching the wire reference; annual sworn declaration of no nominee accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Excessive concentration of revenue in a single non-CAD currency (USD-dominated treasury without a documented FX policy)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal FX risk management policy adopted by the board; hedge documentation with the bank's capital markets desk; USD concentration justification memo referencing contract denomination; monthly CAD-equivalent profit-and-loss reporting; retained-earnings plan for future repatriation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders subscribe shares of the BC corporation by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the corporate operating account, with field 70 narrative 'Capital subscription - share issuance under BCBCA'. The receiving bank completes FINTRAC cross-border EFT reporting for receipts exceeding CAD 10,000. Supporting documents: board resolution authorizing share issuance, share subscription agreement, UBO KYC dossier, and source-of-funds declaration. No Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control filing is required; the injected capital is credited to share capital and contributed surplus on the CRA corporate ledger, with a tax memo distinguishing equity injection from taxable income to prevent Income Tax Act mischaracterization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service-based payables (freelance CAD drafters, structural engineering subcontractors, software subscriptions) are settled via (i) SWIFT MT103 corporate wires for high-value invoices and statutory-subject payments; (ii) Wise Business batch payment rail for low-value recurring disbursements across CAD/USD/EUR corridors, subject to archiving of subcontractor contracts and itemized invoices; (iii) commercial letters of credit are structurally disfavored for pure engineering services because no bill of lading or documentary title exists, and are not recommended unless mandated by a client procurement rule; (iv) corporate purchasing cards are acceptable for SaaS tools (Autodesk BIM, structural analysis platforms); (v) a disciplined wire-reference standard (e.g., 'INV-2024-XXXX-BIM') must be applied to all outgoing payments to prevent false FINTRAC alerts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD spot and outright forwards up to 24 months under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex;
Deliverable FX swaps (repeated rollovers of forward contracts) to manage the timing of monthly USD revenue repatriation;
OTC European-style FX call and put options on CAD/USD to cap repatriation cost while preserving upside;
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible strictly for residual CNY, PHP, or INR exposure where the underlying currency is non-deliverable in Canada;
Cross-currency swaps (CAD-linked interest rate swap with a USD leg) for future acquisition funding or long-term debt restructuring, subject to bank credit approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report for Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - British Columbia Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of the company's date of incorporation; e.g., an incorporation anniversary of 15 March requires filing on or before 15 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the window places the company in non-compliance and blocks issuance of a Certificate of Good Standing. If annual reports remain unfiled for two consecutive years, the Registrar may issue a notice of intent to strike off and, after the notice period, administratively dissolve the company. Restoration requires an application, court order where applicable, and payment of all outstanding fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including corporate annual info)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year corporation, no later than 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Income Tax Act: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; arrears interest compounds daily; repeated failures attract additional penalties. Failure to file may also lead to a CRA compliance order and director liability for unpaid amounts in some cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset thresholds mandate an independent audit for a private BC business corporation. An independent audit is mandatory only if the company is a public company or reporting issuer under the BC Securities Act, or if shareholders pass an ordinary resolution requiring the appointment of an auditor. For a private engineering/CAD outsourcing company, audit is voluntary and may be waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private BC corporations report under Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), CPA Canada Handbook Part II. Public enterprises and reporting issuers must apply IFRS. Tax returns are prepared on the CRA tax basis under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a BC provincial corporation there is no annual UBO confirmation filing to the Registrar. The company must maintain an up-to-date register of members; every share transfer must be recorded in the register as it occurs. The directors must ensure the register is accurate and available for inspection; any transfer that changes control is reflected in the company's records. If the entity were a CBCA (federal) corporation, the Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be reviewed and updated at least annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal general Part I rate + 12% British Columbia provincial general rate); 11% combined (9% federal + 2% BC) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canada-controlled private corporation (CCPC).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credits: 33.33% fully refundable (CCPC, first CAD 3,000,000 expenditure limit) or 15% non-refundable (non-CCPC), plus the BC SR&ED tax credit; federal small business deduction; immediate expensing under CCA Class 56 for software/data infrastructure; no general territorial exemption - worldwide income taxed with foreign tax credits (Schedule 21).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (integrated federal and BC returns, including BC Schedule 5); filed through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) 'My Business Account' or a registered EFILE service provider; GIFI Schedule 125 and capital cost allowance (CCA) schedules embedded; electronic filing is mandatory for corporations with gross revenue over CAD 1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing-due date is 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 December year-end due 30 June); balance-due date is 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months after year-end for CCPCs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, 9-digit Business Number (BN) with 4-digit program account code RC0001, jurisdiction of incorporation (Federal or BC), fiscal period start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State country of control; if 25% or more of shares controlled by non-residents, note that the SBD is denied and Schedule 9 (NRO/foreign affiliate status) must be reviewed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) for income tax purposes: accounting profit reconciled by adding non-deductible expenses (e.g., 50% meals, excessive interest under s. 18(1)(b) thin-capitalization) and deducting items such as allowable capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income for residency purposes; claim foreign tax credits (Schedule 21) for taxes paid to the offshore BIM delivery jurisdiction; verify that the CRA does not deem the entity non-resident under the 'mind and management' test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after application of non-capital losses (20-year carry-forward/3-year carry-back), charitable donation carry-over, and the provinces' income allocation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a BC-resident corporation, allocate income to BC based on the permanent establishment formula; a pure offshore-delivery company with no BC PE must still file and may allocate 0% only with compliant books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax: 38% basic rate less 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction equals 15% headline; SBD on the first CAD 500,000 of Canadian active business income at 9%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The provincial abatement is not available for foreign-source business income; maintain a separate computation for non-Canadian income and verify treaty residency to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC taxable income and BC corporate income tax at 12% general rate; BC small business deduction reduces the rate to 2% on the first CAD 500,000 of eligible income; BC loss carry-overs mirrored from the T2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the corporation is resident in BC but conducts the BIM/CAD work offshore, ensure no sales or services are attributed to a foreign branch; otherwise, the BC allocation ratio must be amended.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); repeat non-filer: 10% plus 2% per month; daily interest on unpaid balances at the prescribed rate plus 4%; failure to file T106: CAD 250/day up to CAD 25,000; false or grossly negligent returns: 50% civil penalty (s. 163(2)).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents; CRA e-file using approved electronic format; attached to or filed alongside the T2.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the same day as the T2 (6 months after fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business number of the reporting corporation, name and country of each non-resident transacting party, relationship description, and the non-resident's tax identification number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List every non-arm's-length party (e.g., foreign BIM offshore service provider) with transactions in the fiscal year; do not net purchases against sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate CAD amounts of goods, services, interest, royalties, rents, management fees, and intercompany debt with each non-resident; identify the transfer-pricing method used (CUP, Resale, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report amounts in Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada annual exchange rate; accuracy is essential because CRA compares T106 data against OFDI and foreign affiliate filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contemporaneous arm's-length analysis: functional/risk profile of the Canadian entity, comparable benchmark, and reason the selected method is the most reliable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare before the filing deadline; penalty relief under s. 247(3) is lost if documentation is prepared only after CRA audit notification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106: CAD 250/day for each day of default (minimum CAD 2,500, maximum CAD 25,000); failure to produce documentation or a complete transfer-pricing survey: CAD 1,000 per document per month of default (maximum CAD 24,000 per audit cycle); intentional non-disclosure is treated as gross negligence (s. 163(2)) and triggers a 50% penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-resident shareholders (s. 212(2)); BC imposes no additional provincial dividend tax; treaty-reduced rates: 5% for a US corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of voting shares, else 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident payee must file Form NR301 (Claim for a Reduction in the Rate of Non-Resident Tax Withholding) with the CRA before the payment is made and provide a valid Certificate of Residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the US, or the equivalent treaty-competent authority certificate) demonstrating beneficial ownership and full economic substance; the payer may then withhold the treaty rate and file a T4NR/NR4 Summary with NR4 slips; absent a valid NR301/TRC, the payer must withhold 25% and remains jointly and severally liable for any shortfall.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties (software/IP, patents, industrial know-how) and rent/royalty for the use of property: statutory 25% Part XIII; treaty rates commonly 0% (Canada-US copyright/software), 10%-15% (industrial royalties under most DTAs). Interest: statutory 25% with the 'exempt interest' carve-out for arm's-length long-term debt; treaty rates usually 0% for arm's-length interest (Canada-US) and 10%-15% for related-party or back-to-back arrangements. SR&ED-eligible payments and cost-sharing arrangements must be documented separately to avoid re-characterization as royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 reporting threshold: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate arm's-length value of goods and/or CAD 50,000 of services, interest, rents, royalties and other transactions with any one non-resident in a taxation year; CRA requires full contemporaneous documentation under s. 247(4) whenever transactions are priced between related parties, regardless of dollar value, and treats the taxpayer as bearing the burden of proof for penalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations are not legislated in Canada; instead the CRA applies (i) the OECD place-of-effective-management (POEM) residency test, (ii) GAAR (s. 245) to artificial transactions, (iii) s. 247(2)(b) re-characterization of commercially irrational cross-border structures, and (iv) bare-bones 'mailbox' entities are disregarded for treaty entitlement under the Multilateral Convention (BEPS MLI Article 7/9, beneficial-ownership rules). A BC corporation performing civil-infrastructure CAD/BIM services must maintain employees, decision-making, risk-taking and bank-account control in BC for each invoiced project.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully evading taxes by omitting invoices, recording fake subcontractor costs, maintaining undisclosed foreign bank/Wise accounts, or instructing an accountant to file a false T2 (s. 239(1) and s. 163(2)).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable offence: a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; summary conviction: 50%-200% fine and imprisonment up to 2 years; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax; CRA criminal referral to the Public Prosecution Service of Canada and publication of convicted taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in or consented to the false return face personal criminal charges, personal restitution orders, seizure of personal assets, prohibition on leaving Canada upon criminal indictment, and, after conviction, a travel ban; the corporate veil is pierced under the doctrine of fraud.
